## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A 7-fascicle systematic doctrinal compendium by [窺基](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%AA%BA%E5%9F%BA) **Kuījī** (632–682), the chief disciple of [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) and the formal founder of the **Cí'ēn 慈恩 / Fǎxiàng 法相** school. The single most important Cí'ēn-school doctrinal-essay collection of the Táng. Preserved in the *Taishō* at T45n1861. Companion volumes by Kuījī's disciples: [KR6n0125](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0125) *Bǔquè* 補闕 by [慧沼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E6%B2%BC) (X55n0882) and [KR6n0126](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0126) *Juézé jì* 決擇記 by [智周](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E5%91%A8) (X55n0883).

**Abstract**

The *Yìlín zhāng* is the canonical Cí'ēn-school doctrinal compendium, designed to lay out the complete Yogācāra doctrinal system in the form of a series of definitional essays organised by topic rather than by sūtra. It is the immediate Chinese equivalent of an Indian *abhidharma-kośa*-style systematic treatise but addressed specifically to the Yogācāra-Cí'ēn synthesis as transmitted by [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) from Nālandā. Topics covered include the eight consciousnesses, the three natures (*sān xìng* 三性), the *èr kōng* (twofold emptiness), the *èr zhàng* (twofold obscuration), the bodhisattva-stages, the path-doctrine, and a substantial number of more specialised technical topics (the *bāshí guījǔ*, the four-fold investigation of the cognitive object, etc.). It is the single most-cited Cí'ēn-school work after the *Chéng wéishí lùn* itself, and the principal source-of-record for the Cí'ēn-school's settled positions on most doctrinal questions.

The dating window 660–682 brackets Kuījī's productive Cí'ēnsì period from his establishment as senior translator-disciple of [玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98) (post-660) through to his death in 682. Wilkinson, *Chinese History*, treats the Táng Yogācāra synthesis under §§ 33–34 of the Buddhist sections; the *Yìlín zhāng* is the principal Chinese-language reference for that synthesis. The work was extensively commented on in Sino-Japanese tradition: the most important sub-commentaries are [KR6n0125](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6n/KR6n0125) *Bǔquè* by [慧沼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%85%A7%E6%B2%BC) (Kuījī's disciple) and the parallel Japanese Hossō sub-commentaries (T71n2317 etc.) preserved in the *Taishō*.
